fixed.ground_and_flora: open ground in front of the March Hare's house under one large, full-leafed shade tree (designed: a horse-chestnut in dark July leaf); the long table in dappled shade; dry summer grass beyond the shade in full sun; the fur-thatched roof sun-warmed
fixed.dream_growth: Grows from the household's fixed tea-time, which Alice is late for when she wakes (cp-tea). The Hatter's 'always six o'clock' is the tea-time she is sleeping through. The light is the real late afternoon over the bank: warm, slanting, unchanging while the party goes round the table.
fixed.dream_clock_note: Inside the dream the clock is stuck at six (ch007-p57, 'It's always six o'clock now'). The Hatter's watch shows the day of the month, not the hour (ch007-p27). On 4 July, six o'clock light and the waking-clock light here (about 17:14-17:33, within half an hour of six) are both late afternoon with the sun still well up, so the two readings agree.
